issues.claim: NCDC 2019: wash every wound under running tap water with soap for up to 15 minutes, as soon as possible.
issues.problem: 'Up to 15 minutes' reads as a maximum, implying a shorter wash is acceptable. NCDC 2019 Table 1 and Table 2 say 'for 15 minutes', and the NCDC Rabies PEP Protocol chart printed in the same guideline says 'for at least 15 minutes'. Only the running text of §2.6.1.1 says 'desirable up to 15 minutes'. WHO TRS 1012 says approximately 15 minutes.
issues.correction: NCDC 2019: wash every wound with soap under running tap water for 15 minutes (the NCDC PEP protocol chart says at least 15 minutes), as soon as possible. WHO TRS 1012: approximately 15 minutes.
issues.evidence: NCDC National Guidelines for Rabies Prophylaxis 2019 (https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/uploads/resource/1769332447_National-Guidelines-for-Rabies-Prophylaxis.pdf), Table 2, p. 6: 'Wash all wounds under running tap water with soap for 15 minutes.' Table 1, p. 5: 'Wash exposed areas with soap and running water for 15 minutes and then apply antiseptic'. Rabies PEP protocol chart (PDF p. 48): 'Gently wash all scratches or wounds with mild soap and running water for at least "15 minutes"'. WHO TRS 1012 §8.3, p. 60: 'thorough washing and flushing of the wound for approximately 15 min with soap and copious amounts of water is required.'

issues.claim: Tetanus interval after bites: IDSA 2014 — toxoid if none within 10 years; CDC — bites are dirty wounds, booster if 5 or more years.
issues.problem: This presents IDSA 2014 as a 10-year rule for bites that conflicts with CDC's 5-year rule. That quotes only the IDSA recommendation sentence. IDSA's own evidence summary for Q XIII applies the 5-year interval to dirty wounds and 10 years to clean wounds. A reader could skip a booster 5–10 years after the last dose for a bite (a dirty wound) on IDSA's authority.
issues.correction: Tetanus after bites: IDSA 2014 recommends toxoid if none within 10 years (Tdap preferred if never given), and its supporting text adds a booster for dirty wounds if >5 years since the last dose. CDC classes bites as dirty wounds: booster if 5 or more years.
issues.evidence: IDSA 2014 SSTI guideline, Q XIII (https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/skin-and-soft-tissue-infections/ ; doi:10.1093/cid/ciu296). Recommendation: 'Tetanus toxoid should be administered to patients without toxoid vaccination within 10 years.' Evidence summary: 'A booster dose of tetanus toxoid vaccine should be administered for dirty wounds if >5 years has elapsed since the last dose and for clean wounds, if >10 years.'

issues.claim: Bites: IDSA 2014 gives tetanus toxoid if none within 10 years (Tdap preferred if never given); CDC classes saliva-contaminated wounds, including bites, as dirty — vaccine if the last dose was 5 or more years ago.
issues.problem: Same as in the rabies protocol: IDSA's supporting text for this question applies a >5-year interval to dirty wounds, so IDSA does not actually support a 10-year interval for a dirty bite wound. Presenting it as a 10-year alternative risks a missed booster 5–10 years after the last dose.
issues.correction: Bites: IDSA 2014 recommends tetanus toxoid if none within 10 years (Tdap preferred if never given), and its supporting text gives a booster for dirty wounds if >5 years since the last dose. CDC classes saliva-contaminated wounds, including bites, as dirty: vaccine if the last dose was 5 or more years ago.
issues.evidence: IDSA 2014, Q XIII evidence summary (https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/skin-and-soft-tissue-infections/): 'A booster dose of tetanus toxoid vaccine should be administered for dirty wounds if >5 years has elapsed since the last dose and for clean wounds, if >10 years. Tdap is preferred over Td if the former has not been previously given.'

issues.claim: WHO 2017: primary doses at least 4 weeks apart (first to second) and at least 6 months apart (second to third).
issues.problem: WHO 2017 gives the 4-week / 6-month spacing under 'Primary and catch-up schedule in children ≥1 year, adolescents and adults'. For infants, WHO's primary series uses a minimum of 4 weeks between every dose, with the third dose completed by 6 months of age if possible. As written, the rule applies to all ages and would delay the third primary dose in an infant by months.
issues.correction: WHO 2017 (catch-up in children ≥1 year, adolescents and adults): first and second doses at least 4 weeks apart, second and third at least 6 months apart. For infants, at least 4 weeks between each of the 3 primary doses (UIP: pentavalent at 6, 10 and 14 weeks).
issues.evidence: WHO tetanus position paper, WER 2017;92(6), p. 72, under 'Primary and catch-up schedule in children ≥1 year, adolescents and adults': 'For primary immunization the first and second doses should be delivered with an interval of at least 4 weeks, and the second and third with an interval of at least 6 months.' p. 71, 'Primary vaccination and booster doses in children': 'A primary series of 3 doses of TTCV is recommended, with the first dose administered from 6 weeks of age. Subsequent doses should be given with a minimum interval of 4 weeks between doses. The third dose of the primary series should be completed by 6 months of age if possible.' (https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/755f3823-3c9a-47e7-b4c5-0fa61d2400d2/content)

issues.claim: StepDose 'Rabies human monoclonal antibody, Serum Institute (Rabishield) — Lancet 2025': WeightDose(3.33, 3.33, IU), note = "Approved in India in 2016 (Lancet 2025); not in the NCDC 2019 national guidelines"
issues.problem: The manufacturer's product information is findable online and confirms the 3.33 IU/kg dose. It also lists two strengths, 40 IU/mL and 100 IU/mL, a 2.5-fold difference in volume per IU that the note omits (the Twinrab entry does give its strengths). The manufacturer also directs any remaining volume IM at a site distant from the vaccine, whereas the Lancet trial infiltrated the wounds only. No CDSCO approval text or package insert with the dose was found.
issues.correction: Add to the note: 'Manufacturer: 3.33 IU/kg; vials 100 IU/2.5 mL (40 IU/mL) and 250 IU/2.5 mL (100 IU/mL) — check the vial; any remaining volume IM at a site distant from the vaccine.' Cite the Serum Institute Rabishield product page (https://seruminstitute.com/product_ind_rabishield.php) as a source.
issues.evidence: Serum Institute of India, Rabishield product page (https://seruminstitute.com/product_ind_rabishield.php): 'The recommended dose of Rabishield is 3.33 IU/kg body Weight'; 'PRESENTATION: 100 IU/ 2.5 ml (40 IU/ml) vial; 250 IU/2.5 ml (100 IU/ml) vial'; 'If anatomically feasible, the full dose of Rabishield should be thoroughly infiltrated in the area around and into the wounds. Any remaining volume Should be injected intramuscularly at a site distant from vaccine administration.' Lancet 2025 abstract (PMID 40783290): 'RmAb (3·33 IU/kg) and ERIG (40 IU/kg) were infiltrated into and around the wounds only on day 0'.
